decisions.reason: As a visible extension of the established geospatial software offer, Product A likely meets at least a minimum aspiration level for a first-year launch and is worth retaining while market feedback accumulates.

Product B fits the firm's strategic move toward integrated, user-centered geospatial enterprise solutions, and in a growing market a medium-sized R&D-active firm would usually give such a new service more time before judging it below aspiration.

Because Product C is close to the firm's existing capabilities and supports secure integration in enterprise environments, management would likely keep it under initial uncertainty rather than redeploy resources prematurely.

Product D strengthens the firm's platform and development ecosystem around GIS applications, so with organisational slack and no clear sign of failure it would be kept for further learning and customer adoption.
Product E received an explicit launch push on the website and aligns closely with demand for secure GeoIT integration, so its early results would likely be judged promising enough to continue.
